title: AI Datasets
answer: Training and evaluation datasets with size, licence, provenance, language coverage, and documented bias.

reading.body:
The dataset layer of AI is organized around three questions: what a model trains on, what it is tested against, and what may lawfully be used.

Training corpora carry provenance and licence as first-class attributes, not footnotes. Evaluation sets are defined by what they actually measure, which is a narrower claim than what they are often reported to measure. Licensing and provenance sit alongside both, because the same corpus can be permissible for one use and not another.

For AI specifically, this is the input side of the compute story. Compute determines how large a model can be, but the data determines what that compute is spent learning and what the resulting model can be said to do. A benchmark that measures something other than its name suggests propagates error into every capability claim built on it.

The data does not say how many datasets exist, who holds them, or how coverage varies by language. It names the categories and their concerns, and nothing about their contents.
